description: Anatomy opens an interactive 3D human body inside ChatGPT. Ask about a muscle, bone, nerve, joint or organ and ChatGPT frames it, fades whatever covers it, and labels what matters. Peel away muscle layers, cut through the body, isolate a structure, colour-code what belongs together, and play movements like bending, squatting or lifting a knee. Anatomy can also draw a muscle's line of pull across the hip or knee, so you can watch a muscle change its job as the joint moves. Tap anything to ask about it, mark where something hurts, or ask for a quick find-it quiz. Anatomy shows reference anatomy for learning and explanation; it does not diagnose or give medical advice.

defaultPrompt: My buttock aches and it runs down the back of my thigh. Show me the piriformis and the sciatic nerve.
A PT said my piriformis switches jobs when my hip is bent. Show me what it does as I lift my knee.
Quiz me on the rotator cuff. Make me find each muscle on the model.

positive.description: Show a structure and what covers it
positive.prompt: I get a deep ache in my right buttock that sometimes runs down the back of my thigh. Show me the piriformis and the sciatic nerve so I can see how they sit.
positive.expected_behavior: Looks up the exact structure names with find_anatomy, then opens the 3D viewer on the right buttock from behind: piriformis and sciatic nerve coloured and labelled, gluteus maximus faded so both are visible. The reply explains that the nerve usually passes below the muscle and does not diagnose the ache.

positive.prompt: Show me the rotator cuff from behind and colour each muscle differently.
positive.expected_behavior: Looks up the four rotator cuff muscles, then opens the viewer on both shoulders from behind with supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis each in a different colour and a legend naming them. The reply notes that subscapularis lies on the front of the shoulder blade.

positive.description: Show a muscle changing its action as a joint moves
positive.prompt: What does the piriformis do as I lift my knee toward my chest? Show me.
positive.expected_behavior: Looks up the piriformis, then opens the viewer on the right hip from behind playing a knee-to-chest movement from 0 to 100 degrees of hip flexion with a scrubber, and draws the piriformis line of pull with a readout of its actions. The reply explains that it rotates the thigh outward when standing and that this changes as the hip bends.

positive.prompt: Show me the L4-L5 disc from above with the body cut through it so I can see where the nerves sit.
positive.expected_behavior: Looks up the disc, vertebrae and lumbar nerve roots, then opens the viewer looking straight down on a horizontal cut through the L4-L5 disc, with the disc and the nerves in the spinal canal coloured and labelled and a cut slider shown. The reply explains that the disc sits in front of the canal and the nerve roots run behind and out to the sides.

positive.prompt: Quiz me on the hip muscles. Make me find them on the model.
positive.expected_behavior: Looks up the hip muscles, then opens the viewer in quiz mode on the hip with labels hidden, asking the person to tap each named muscle in turn (for example "Find the gluteus maximus", 1 of 8). Correct and wrong taps are shown and the answer is revealed after two tries. The reply lists the muscles in the quiz.

negative.description: Do not invoke for medication dosing questions.
negative.prompt: How much ibuprofen can I safely take in a day?

negative.description: Do not invoke for finding or booking a clinician.
negative.prompt: Find me a physiotherapist near me who is open on Saturdays.

negative.description: Do not invoke for general health numbers that need no visual.
negative.prompt: What is a normal resting heart rate for a 30 year old?

publication.release_notes: Adds sign-in with Google, or with email and password for accounts we create. Signed-in tool calls carry a one-sentence reason from the assistant that is stored with the account. Adds a tool to permanently delete your Anatomy account. The viewer checks for updates less often and stops while the tab is hidden.
